title: Impact of Credit Score Threshold on Loan Default Rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
The study will employ Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) to determine the causal impact of crossing a credit score threshold on loan default rates. RDD is appropriate here because we are exploiting the discontinuity at the credit score threshold to estimate the local average treatment effect. The key assumption of RDD is that individuals just above and below the cutoff are similar except for the treatment assignment, allowing us to attribute any discontinuous jump in the outcome to the treatment.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(rdrobust)

# Read the data
data_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s89_data.csv"
data <- read.csv(data_path)

# Ensure 'treated' and 'near_cutoff' are factors
data$treated <- as.factor(data$treated)
data$near_cutoff <- as.factor(data$near_cutoff)

# Plot the running variable vs. outcome for visualization
ggplot(data, aes(x = running_var, y = y, color = treated)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Default Rate vs Credit Score",
       x = "Credit Score",
       y = "Default Rate")

# Implement RDD using the rdrobust package
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = 0.5)

# Print the results
print(rdd_result)

# Conduct basic robustness checks: sensitivity to bandwidth selection
rdd_result_bw1 <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = 0.5, h = 0.1)
rdd_result_bw2 <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = 0.5, h = 0.05)

# Print the robustness check results
cat("\nRDD Result with bandwidth 0.1:\n")
print(rdd_result_bw1)
cat("\nRDD Result with bandwidth 0.05:\n")
print(rdd_result_bw2)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a negative sign for the treatment effect of crossing the credit score threshold on loan default rates, meaning getting approved (having a credit score above the threshold) is likely associated with a lower likelihood of default. This expectation is based on the theoretical understanding that loan approval entails the borrower's strength in meeting repayment obligations, reducing the probability of default. The magnitude of the effect will depend on the precise position of the threshold and the variability in scores nearby; thus, an approximate magnitude might range from moderate to strong depending on the variation and discontinuity strength.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The analysis exploits the discontinuity at the credit score threshold to identify the causal effect.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Crossing the credit score threshold increases the default rate.
